body.statement: There exists \(C<\infty\) such that the certified finite-profile algorithm terminates for every sample and returns \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) with \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}=\bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\subseteq\mathcal M\). For every \(a\in I\) and \(b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\), \(\{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a)\). Whenever \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\neq\varnothing\), the outward endpoint evaluations satisfy \(0\le\inf_{Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\le C\zeta_n\) and \(0\le\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\sup_{Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)\le C\zeta_n=o(r_n)\), uniformly over \(a\in I\). Moreover, \(|\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le\exp\{C K_n^2\log(K_n/\zeta_n)\}\).
body.justification: Honesty is operational only if every continuum restriction and endpoint is enclosed by a checkable finite certificate.
body.gap: Kato, Sasaki, and Ura implement a finite frequency inversion but do not certify equivalence to a continuum profile; Neumann uses a continuous metric without a finite outer optimization.
body.consumer: Empirical users obtain reproducible band endpoints whose numerical error is asymptotically negligible relative to statistical width.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the claim by making explicit the compactness and enclosure facts used by the stated algorithm.  First, for \(h\) supported on \(\mathcal A\) with \(\|h\|_{H^\beta}\le R\), Fourier inversion and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \|h\|_\infty\le C R,
 \qquad
 |h(a)-h(a')|\le C R|a-a'|^{\beta-1/2\wedge1}.
\]
More generally, truncating the Fourier integral at frequency \(T\) gives a uniform remainder at most \(CRT^{1/2-\beta}\).  Thus the density and marked-density balls, restricted to \(I\), are totally bounded in the uniform norm.  A Fourier mesh followed by outward interval rounding gives, at accuracy \(u\), at most
\[
 \exp\{C u^{-1/(\beta-1/2)}\log(C/u)\} \tag{30}
\]
boxes.  This count follows by taking \(T\asymp u^{-1/(\beta-1/2)}\), using mesh width of order \(u/T\), and quantizing each bounded Fourier coefficient outward.

Second, Markov's inequality applied to the error second moments gives
\[
 Q(|U_j|>T)\le M_e/T^2. \tag{31}
\]
On \([-T,T]\), positive quadrature exact for monomials through order \(2K_n\) is obtained directly as follows.  The moment vector lies in the convex hull of the moment curve \((1,u,\ldots,u^{2K_n})\).  If a convex representation has more than \(2K_n+2\) support points, affine dependence permits one weight to be reduced to zero without changing the vector; iteration leaves at most \(2K_n+2\) positive atoms.  Taylor's formula encloses the exponential remainder, while (31) encloses the two tails.  Subdivision of atom locations, weights, tails, and remainder values therefore gives finite outward boxes for both error transforms.  Products and integrals are enclosed by the natural complex interval operations.  The same argument applies simultaneously to every stratum and to the probability and marked channels.

The algorithm retains a box only with its outward constraint certificate and subdivides until the radius of every constraint and objective interval is at most \(\zeta_n\).  Total boundedness of the preceding parameter sets implies that a finite subdivision attains this tolerance.  Every exact candidate \(Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) belongs to one of the boxes because Taylor, tail, quadrature, and rounding intervals were all taken outward.  Hence
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq
 \bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)
 =\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal M. \tag{32}
\]
The last inclusion holds because the decoder admits only laws in \(\mathcal M\).  Interval evaluation preserves inclusion under addition, multiplication, and division whenever the denominator interval is bounded away from zero.  Here that division is valid because it is intersected with \([\kappa,\infty)\).  Thus
\[
 \{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a). \tag{33}
\]

For a retained box meeting the exact profile, every value of its objective interval differs by at most \(C\zeta_n\) from the objective of a represented exact-profile law.  Boxes certified disjoint from the constraint set are discarded.  Applying this fact to the boxes containing minimizers and maximizers, and using compactness to pass to a minimizing or maximizing subsequence, gives uniformly in \(a\in I\)
\[
 0\le\inf_{Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)-\underline m_n^{\mathrm{cert}}(a)
 \le C\zeta_n,
\]
\[
 0\le\overline m_n^{\mathrm{cert}}(a)-\sup_{Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)
 \le C\zeta_n. \tag{34}
\]
These statements are conditional only on nonemptiness of the exact profile, as required.

It remains to check the announced finite size.  For sufficiently large \(n\), the definition of \(K_n\) implies
\[
 \log(en)\asymp K_n\log K_n,
 \qquad
 \zeta_n\asymp K_n^{-\beta-1/2}(\log K_n)^{-1}. \tag{35}
\]
Because \(\beta>3/2\),
\[
 \zeta_n^{-1/(\beta-1/2)}\log(C/\zeta_n)
 \le C K_n^2\log(K_n/\zeta_n). \tag{36}
\]
The coefficient, positive-quadrature, tail, and remainder descriptions have at most \(CK_n^2\) scalar coordinates; quantizing each at outward resolution proportional to \(\zeta_n/K_n^2\), and combining (30) and (36), proves
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le
 \exp\{CK_n^2\log(K_n/\zeta_n)\}.
\]
Finally, \(\zeta_n/r_n=1/\log(en)\to0\), so (34) also gives \(C\zeta_n=o(r_n)\).  This proves termination, coverage, endpoint accuracy, and the certificate-count bound.
